channel.title: MYRSS Daily Digest
channel.description: World-affairs reader digest, prioritising the last 48 hours from the seven-day source archive. Two items per publication. Source feeds appear to have been refreshed early on 23 November; later events may be missing. Most summaries are based on RSS metadata; Reuters reports were checked against original articles.

item.title: de Volkskrant | Hevige droneaanvallen op Soedanese hoofdstad Khartoem, ook VN-gebouw getroffen
item.description: De Volkskrant headline reports heavy drone attacks on Sudan's capital Khartoum, including a United Nations building. Based on the RSS headline; damage and casualties not independently verified.

item.title: de Volkskrant | Opnieuw burgerdoden na Russische droneaanvallen op voorsteden Kyiv
item.description: De Volkskrant reports further civilian deaths following Russian drone strikes on suburbs of Kyiv. Based on the RSS headline; no casualty figure independently established.

item.title: New York Times | Behind China’s A.I. Anxieties, Fear of a Nuclear Checkmate
item.description: Chinese military researchers are exploring AI applications while worrying that the technology could make China's nuclear forces more vulnerable to attack. Based on the publisher's RSS summary.

item.title: New York Times | COP31 Talks Collapse in Turkey in a Clash Over Fossil Fuels
item.description: The New York Times reports that COP31 talks in Turkey ended without a political deal after disputes over language on phasing out fossil fuels. Based on the publisher's RSS summary.

item.title: Follow the Money | Paspoorten te koop: Roemenië zette de deur open voor aan het Kremlin gelieerde Russen
item.description: FTM's headline reports that Romania opened a route to passports for Russians linked to the Kremlin. This is the publisher's investigative framing, not an independently verified finding.

item.title: Follow the Money | Hoe cocaïnegeld België binnendringt: ‘Het zat vroeger niet zo diep in het systeem’
item.description: FTM examines how cocaine trafficking proceeds penetrate Belgium's economy and institutions, drawing on interviews with justice officials. Based on the headline and available feed metadata.

item.title: Reuters | Europe's cloud sovereignty push gains ground, but US hyperscalers remain dominant
item.description: Reuters reports growing sovereign-cloud procurement in Europe, including Dutch government contracts, but says US hyperscalers still dominate and migration remains slow. Checked against original Reuters reporting.

item.title: Reuters | Saudi Arabia's influence loomed large over failed COP31 deal
item.description: Reuters reports negotiators' allegations that Saudi Arabia wielded outsized influence against fossil-fuel transition language at COP31. The Turkish presidency denied preferential treatment. Checked against original Reuters reporting.

item.title: The New Yorker | The Mystery of Mercury
item.description: A science feature explores Mercury's extreme surface conditions and ancient crater ice, alongside the BepiColombo mission's arrival in orbit. Based on the publisher's RSS summary.

item.title: The New Yorker | “Out of Time,” by Mary Gaitskill
item.description: New fiction by Mary Gaitskill, reflecting on affection and human connection. A wind-down literary selection; description limited to RSS metadata.
